faq: Can you put a tent on a Riverdale driveway?
Possibly. Paved or stake-restricted sites may need a frame-style or weighted setup. Send the address, surface type, and approximate dimensions so we can confirm the right option.
How much space should I leave around the tent?
The tent footprint is only part of the site plan. We also need working clearance, access, anchoring space where applicable, and room for guest movement.
Can I add tables and chairs to the tent order?
Yes. Downstate service is built around complete event orders, so seating, tables, lighting, linens and other add-ons can be included in the same quote.

globalFaq: What is the Downstate minimum?
Downstate complete-event deliveries generally start around $1,500 before tax. The exact minimum depends on the service zone, date, equipment, access, setup requirements, and pickup plan.
Do you serve every Bronx or Westchester address?
Not automatically. We review the address, order size, route, access, surface, and setup requirements before accepting a Downstate delivery.
Do you set up and take down the equipment?
Accepted tent, inflatable, and complete-event orders include the applicable setup and breakdown plan in the quote. The quote confirms exactly what our crew handles.
Can a pole tent go on concrete or asphalt?
Pole tents are best suited to appropriate grass sites where staking is allowed. Paved or stake-restricted sites may require a frame-style or weighted setup, subject to the equipment and site.
What do you need to approve an inflatable site?
We review usable flat space, gate and carry access, surface, anchoring conditions, overhead clearance, power, and water access when the unit requires water.
Can I rent only a few chairs or one small item?
Small orders may be possible, but the Downstate complete-event delivery minimum still applies. The service is designed primarily for larger coordinated event orders.
How do I know whether a tent will fit?

Send the address, approximate usable dimensions, surface type, guest count, and any layout needs such as buffet space, dance floor, bars, or walkways. We will tell you what else is needed before confirming the setup.
When are delivery and pickup times confirmed?
The delivery, setup, and pickup plan is confirmed in the written quote or booking details after we review the event schedule, location, access, and route.
Can schools, churches, and venues request a certificate of insurance?
Tell us the venue or organization requirements when requesting the quote so we can review what documentation is needed before booking.
Does submitting the quote form reserve the date?
No. A request starts the review process. Equipment, staffing, site suitability, and the event date are confirmed through the booking process.
siteReadiness: Measure the clear area where the tent or inflatable would actually sit—not the entire yard. Include nearby fences, trees, sheds, pools, driveways, and structures.
Tell us whether the site is grass, concrete, asphalt, pavers, mixed surface, or an indoor/venue setup. Surface type affects tent anchoring and inflatable approval.
Note gates, stairs, narrow passages, steep slopes, elevators, long carries, loading docks, or any place large rental equipment must pass through.
Look above and below the site
Flag tree limbs, power lines, roof overhangs, irrigation, septic areas, buried utilities, and other obstacles that can affect tent staking or equipment placement.
Inflatables, lighting, fans, photo booths, and other equipment may need reliable power. Water slides also need a workable water source and hose reach.
Dense Bronx and lower Westchester sites can have limited truck access. Tell us about loading restrictions, parking rules, gates, driveways, and carry distance.
Give us guest arrival, start/end time, venue access time, and any hard setup or pickup restrictions so the crew plan is realistic.
Schools, churches, parks, venues, and managed properties may have rules for insurance, vendors, anchoring, power, access, or operating hours. Send those requirements with the quote request.
